claims.text: Varying the constituent-element composition can tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Composition tuning can enhance the magnetocaloric effect of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Changing alloy composition influences the atomic arrangement of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Changing alloy composition influences the electronic structure of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Composition changes affect magnetic interactions in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Composition changes affect phase stability in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Changes in magnetic interactions influence the magnetocaloric effect.
Changes in phase stability influence the magnetocaloric effect.
An optimized composition will increase the magnetocaloric effect relative to the baseline composition.
An increased magnetocaloric effect will improve performance in low-dimensional applications.
The proposed relationship is limited to non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys and is not asserted for equiatomic or other alloy systems.
The exact relationship between composition and magnetocaloric performance is not fully characterized.
A lack of statistically significant magnetocaloric change across compositions relative to baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
